fieldValues.title: A working group operates independently only in a mature domain
fieldValues.decision_question: Must a domain name its tensions, and what may a working group do in a domain that names fewer than three?
fieldValues.context: 2026-10-17: SP-94 (srs-programme#158). Only Semantic records (12 tensions) and Stance (3) of the seven domains name any trade-offs. Working groups hold domains (holds-domain, D4/D5/D15 ratified 2026-10-16), so a group can be chartered on a domain with nothing to test its decisions against.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Require three tensions before a domain is defined or affirmed (blocks early domains, when we do not yet know their trade-offs). Refuse to charter a group on an immature domain (the group best placed to find the tensions cannot be set up to find them). Never require tensions (decisions in a domain have no default measure for their bias).
fieldValues.decision_statement: Domains mature. A domain may be defined and affirmed without tensions; it is mature when it names at least three tensions (axes). A working group may be set up in an immature domain, but it must establish a mature domain before it can operate independently. Until then it works under the owner: no delegated merges, every PR owner-merged.
fieldValues.rationale: Every solution trades one side of a paradox against the other. The tensions a domain names are its default measurement system: they let a decision say which trade-offs it took and let the group test its bias. A group without them has nothing to judge its own decisions against, so it should not decide alone; but it is often the group that can find them, so it may be set up to do that first.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A group needs independence before three tensions can honestly be named, or three proves the wrong threshold.
